claims: Metformin is a standard type 2 diabetes medication.
Metformin acts directly on the brain to regulate blood sugar, neuroinflammation, and cognitive health.
Recent findings (2026) show metformin works via a hidden pathway in the brain.
Recent findings (2026) show metformin reduces blood sugar by inhibiting a specific protein (Rap1) in neurons.
Metformin reduces neuroinflammation by inhibiting microglia activation.
Studies suggest metformin slows cognitive decline specifically in memory, semantic memory, and executive function, particularly in diabetics.
Metformin was historically thought to act only on peripheral organs (liver/gut).
Metformin's CNS impacts are now recognized.
Metformin is frequently studied for anti-aging effects.
Some studies on young, non-diabetic mice have shown mixed results.
Some studies on young, non-diabetic mice have shown memory impairment under specific conditions.
